sources.title: Nova 2 Lite - Amazon Bedrock
sources.evidence: Names Amazon and Nova 2 Lite, states December 2, 2025 launch and 1M-token context, supports text/image/video input and text output, and identifies nova-2-lite-v1:0 inference profiles. Reasoning and tool use are supported.

sources.title: Amazon Nova 2 Lite - AWS AI Service Cards
sources.evidence: Exact-model service card describes a proprietary foundation model using transformer-based generative machine learning, available under the AWS Customer Agreement or other AWS agreements. It documents optional reasoning, task decomposition, function calling, and multimodal analysis, without parameter counts or dense/MoE classification.

sources.title: Amazon Nova 2: Multimodal Reasoning and Generation Models
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27: the 26-page Amazon AGI technical report identifies Nova 2 Lite as a Nova 2 family model with text/image/video inputs and text output. Its Lite/Pro comparison tables report evaluations, not total or active parameter counts; the searchable text contains no parameter or architecture specification. It identifies no named, size-disclosed base from which Lite inherits a nominal size. The publication page dates the report December 2, 2025.

sources.title: Introducing Amazon Nova 2 Lite, a fast, cost-effective reasoning model
sources.evidence: December 2, 2025 announcement explicitly releases Nova 2 Lite on Bedrock and provides global.amazon.nova-2-lite-v1:0 code. It documents one-million-token context, text/image/video/document inputs, configurable reasoning, function calling, web grounding, and code interpreter.

sources.title: Multimodal understanding - Amazon Nova
sources.evidence: Document section explicitly supports PDF and DOCX visual/text interpretation for Nova 2 Lite. The introduction mentions speech, but the specific video limitations say audio tracks are not processed; the exact Bedrock card and technical report exclude audio input.

sources.title: Migrate from Amazon Nova 1 to Amazon Nova 2 on Amazon Bedrock
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27: the March 18, 2026 Nova 1/Lite comparison table covers context, output, modalities, thinking, tools, and customization, with no total or activated-parameter column. Recommended migrations from Nova 1 Lite, Pro, and Premier are workload upgrades, not a statement that Nova 2 Lite preserves one of their architectures or parameter counts. Document input is supported through Converse, not Invoke.

sources.title: Evaluating Nova 2.0 Lite model under Amazon's Frontier Model Safety Framework
sources.evidence: Later January 2026 Amazon-authored report evaluates Nova 2.0 Lite. It contains no numeric model parameter count or exact dense/MoE classification. Architectural references concern evaluated tasks or general behavior.

sources.title: Amazon Nova 2.5 Sonic - AWS AI Service Cards
sources.evidence: October 5, 2026 sibling card checked for retrospective Nova 2 Lite specifications. It contains no Lite parameter-count comparison; its speech architecture cannot be transferred to Lite.

sources.title: Customize Amazon Nova models with Amazon Bedrock fine-tuning
sources.evidence: April 8, 2026 first-party table compares Nova Premier, Pro, 2 Lite, Lite, and Micro by capabilities, input, output, availability, and customization. It has no total or activated-parameter column. Nova 2 Lite supports SFT and RFT; the post describes customer customization of Nova base models, not a size-bearing predecessor lineage for the released Nova 2 Lite model.

sources.title: What is Amazon Nova 2? - Amazon Nova
sources.evidence: Current developer-guide family table, checked October 27, lists Nova 2 Lite, Nova 2 Sonic, and Nova Multimodal Embeddings by modalities and use cases. It provides no nominal total, activated-parameter count, dense/MoE classification, or named size-disclosed base for Lite.

sources.title: Amazon Nova foundation models
sources.evidence: Current October 27 product page lists Nova 2 Lite alongside Nova 2.5 Sonic and Nova Multimodal Embeddings. Lite specifications cover reasoning, tools, 1M context, and customization; no total/active count or explicit size-bearing base relationship is disclosed.

sources.title: Optimizing LoRA target module selection for efficient fine tuning
sources.evidence: March 19, 2026 study explicitly uses the Nova 2.0 Lite general-availability checkpoint. It names qkv, o_proj, gate_up_proj/fc1, and gate_down_proj/fc2 modules but publishes no nominal total or active count, layer dimensions, or explicit dense/MoE classification. The generic introduction about billions of parameters is not a numeric Lite specification; module and adapter choices do not establish a model count.

sources.title: Customized Amazon Nova models improve molecular-property prediction in drug discovery
sources.evidence: April 15, 2026 study identifies Nova 2 Lite as the base for full-rank supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement fine-tuning. Full-rank refers to updating all model parameters, with no numeric total or active count. This establishes downstream customized-model lineage, not a disclosed-size predecessor of Nova 2 Lite.

name.note: Official display name and v1:0 model identifier agree.

developer.note: Amazon's own model card and Amazon AGI report establish authorship.

family.note: Nova 2 Lite belongs to the Amazon Nova family.

release_date.note: The dated release announcement and Bedrock launch-date field agree; day precision is supported.

open_weights.note: Proprietary model offered as an AWS service; customization access does not establish an open-weight release.

license.note: AWS explicitly calls it proprietary and specifies AWS contractual terms; no open-weight license is asserted.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 searches for nominal counts and named-base lineage, plus reopened exact-model evidence and later first-party comparison tables, found no numeric total. Migration recommendations and customer fine-tuning support do not identify Nova 2 Lite as a size-preserving variant of a disclosed-size base. No supported nominal count is being rejected for lack of an exact tensor census. March LoRA and April molecular-customization studies name the exact base but disclose no numeric model size.

active_parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 review separately sought active or activated counts. The March and April 2026 first-party comparison tables, current family/product pages, exact report/card, later safety report, and Sonic sibling card disclose no Lite active count. Dense/MoE topology and a size-bearing base lineage remain unknown; neither reasoning effort nor a model tier establishes an activated count. The later LoRA study names transformer modules but gives no active count or explicit dense/MoE classification.

architecture.note: The exact service card explicitly establishes transformer-based generation. Dense versus mixture-of-experts and detailed network topology remain undisclosed.

context_window.note: Exact model documentation and launch announcement state one million tokens.

modalities.note: Text/image/video and text output are explicit. PDF is a supported document format via Converse. The generic guide's speech mention conflicts with the exact card/report and is not adopted.

reasoning.note: Optional extended thinking supports low, medium, and high effort; it is disabled by default.

tool_call.note: Function calling and agentic tool use are explicit capabilities.

description.value: Multimodal reasoning model for visual analysis, planning, and tool use
description.note: Supported by documented multimodal reasoning, task decomposition, and tool workflows without benchmark superiority claims.

patch.notes: Transformer-based architecture is documented; total and active parameter counts and dense versus mixture-of-experts classification are undisclosed. PDF input is available through the Converse API; video audio tracks are not processed.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit retains explicit null total and active counts with undisclosed status. Reopened exact-model sources, the January safety report, March migration comparison, and October sibling card; added April customization and current family/product comparisons, plus March LoRA and April molecular-customization studies. No nominal count, activated-parameter column, or named size-disclosed predecessor was found. Prior non-parameter assessments remain unchanged, including documented transformer architecture and PDF-inclusive modalities.
